tips.comment: Leon Trotsky lines up in the 8:00 at Southwell, coming off a confidence-boosting win over this course and distance last month. He seems to have found his stride since stepping up in trip, and with Sean Levey retaining the ride, there’s every chance he can build on that success. If he continues his upward trajectory, he could be a strong contender once again.

Yet to win in 20 starts, but surely will be winning soon, and tonight could be the night. Two eye-catching runs at the start of this year when staying on best late on. Got no luck last time, but upped back to 2 miles here, can be staying on best at the end of the race. Nap at 9/2.
Fiftyshadesaresdev has run well in both starts this year. Third here, then runner-up at Newcastle. That level of form will make the selection competitive against the short-priced favorite.

Toby Tops relevant recent runs have been in 4k avg class, whereas the avg of the rest of the runners is 3.26k (Dropping in class (on average) today). Ranking the 24 relevant recent run class ratings of the entire field shows Toby Tops as running in the 3rd, 3rd, 3rd, and 3rd most difficult recent races. Ranking the 24 relevant recent form ratings of the entire field shows Toby Tops as having the 3rd, 12th, 8th, and 9th best ratings. Bet. (KEY - Best Avg Rating, Southwell (AW) Flat.) (2m½f (2m102y) Gamble Responsibly At BetUK Handicap (Class 6) (4yo+ 0-55)).

OCEAN RIDGE has a fairly horrible profile to be honest but the 5-y-o has at least won a race here before. That was a year ago and although often running a fair race, pickings have been poor since. Still, his new handler is in grand form, this is a further drop in the weights and more interestingly, this is a big step up in distance. Horses have certainly improved before switching from 12f to 16f, so maybe a small interest at a price could reward.
A bit long in the tooth now, but well handicapped on some past performances. Seemingly unfancied, but this ain't a great race. If on song and if it runs its race, well up there.

SCYLLA probably doesn't deserve to be quite as big in the market of this rather poor staying handicap. Able to race into the low 60's in terms of RPRs in 2024, the drop below a mark of 50 for the first time, coupled with blinkers going on, predictably led to a better performance at Wolves earlier this month. Left on the same mark, a decent effort really ought to follow, providing the blinkers have a similar effect. Marco Ghiani retains the ride.

This is a poor Class 6 handicap over 2 miles, and there are 10 runners going to post. I must admit the price has tempted me in for a small each-way play on Kittens Dream. Do I think he will win? Not really, but he could place for a canny return. He hasn't won for 38 runs since 21 Feb 2023, with Dale Swift in the saddle that day. This is the first time that Dale has been back in the saddle since April 2023, and I hope that's an omen for the course and distance winner, racing off joint bottom weight. I think if he is going to run well anywhere, then it will be here at this track for the owners, the Southwell Racing Club.

Sevensees has been shaping up nicely, especially with that recent win at Southwell over this trip earlier in the month. He handled the surface well and looked to have more in the tank, which makes him pretty interesting back at the same track and distance tonight. Definitely one to keep on side if he turns up in the same mood.
Both career wins and several other good efforts over today's course and distance, including latest when looking unlucky. Back up into Class 4 company but can make his presence felt.

Ready Freddie Go has shown strong potential, with 9 wins from 35 runs, including victories on similar ground and surface. He's been a previous winner in this class, and is capable of returning to form.

Still sits 7 lbs above his last winning mark. To be fair, the way he won on that occasion would suggest he's still got plenty to give off a mark like this. He drops back in trip this time, having pulled up in the Edinburgh National last time out. Clearly didn't stay the trip. He bolted up on his second chase run at Wetherby, absolutely battering Farnoge, with a 15L gap separating them at the finish. He's yet to show that form in his two runs since. For me, he had his excuses: non-stayer last time out, and outclassed in a Grade 2 novice the run before that. He gets his beloved quicker ground today. All his best form has come on quicker ground. He won both of his points runs, so clearly made for chasing. If he can get back to his old form, I think he can win again off this mark.

Lucinda Russell may have this sown up with her two runners. YOUR OWN STORY won't go off at 9/2 in my view, and he looks the pick of the pair at the early prices. A consistent chaser who probably has no stamina limitations, this trip is going to be short enough, but the small field and change of headgear may just see the 9-year-old enjoy himself. He has a nice low weight, and although he handles softer, it doesn't seem to matter too much what the ground is like. Hopefully, his rider will take the trouble to weigh in and secure prize money, wherever the pairing finishes.
If Mr. Incredible is sound of mind and body, then he has a decent chance here, as somewhere there is a class horse and a class performance waiting to happen.
Consistent performer who sets a high standard. Dropped in grade and should be straightforward. Has impressive form on good ground and looks to be solid at even money.
Has been running well this season and looks like an improving type. Has won a maiden hurdle and was 2nd on handicap debut. More to come here at a big price.

Third of sixteen over course and distance off this mark of 109 and under today's jockey Brian Hughes in April 2024 on soft ground, weakening on the run in. He won his next race at Perth over a furlong shorter off a pound higher mark in May 2024 and not seen again until November 2024. He has disappointed in all 4 starts since that win at Perth but has been racing off higher marks, will strip fitter for those runs and of interest back below that winning mark.

Looks the correct price, so not much face value. However, the favorite (who looks the most likely winner) trainer is out of form, and that may mean it won't run to form. This could easily pick up the pieces ahead of the rest, and a safety net of 5 places, in my opinion, makes it a good bet.

Interesting price here for a horse who won last time out at Doncaster by two lengths when wearing cheekpieces. This is because Ashington has only worn them twice so far and won the previous time also when form was also hit and miss at that point. Up 4 lbs here, but could be an each-way opportunity.

Whilst I appreciate the fact that this horse is 9lb higher in the handicap now than when winning over C&D on her last visit to the course, there's no getting away from how well she seemed suited by it and how well she won. The same jockey is back on board now, and he's been excelling for this trainer. He's not been on board for the horse's 2 runs since, but he's back on here, and the horse has been freshened up with a little break. Could go well off bottom weight and looks overpriced to me.

A fairly wide open heat, and a chance taken on Ridin Solo who has been beaten off this mark but gets an added claim of 5 lbs from Charlie Maggs. He’s gone well fairly consistently, and I think there’s enough in his form to suggest he can make an impact off an adjusted mark of 100 and from bottom weight in here. He’s unlikely to get a solo up front, but a light weight and front-running tactics could have some of these at it from a fair way out with the right fractions. 4/5 a place on undulating tracks, and 4/5 a place with an uphill finish adds to the intrigue for me, and he won’t mind any extra rain.

The trainer's runners are on fire at the moment, and Feargal has been using the wind op well on many of his winners. It's a tool that he's been using to good effect for sure. This mare was actually having her second wind op before her run last time out, which was an easy win in a maiden hurdle where the third has since won off a 5lb higher mark than Northern Air races off here. The fourth and fifth have also won since too. This all looks like good enough form to take this off this lenient-looking mark.

Has 1 win and 2 placed efforts from 4 runs over hurdles this season. Win came on good at Uttoxeter over 16f with placed runs at Wincanton over 15.5f on good to soft and 23 days ago at Ludlow over 16f on soft, showing ground versatility. Has had a second wind operation since last run and makes the very long journey from D. Pipe's yard with the in-form J. Tudor booked for the ride.

A little overpriced in my opinion and going quite safe. It doesn't seem to have any concerns and hopefully should run its race. Should be around 8/1 but has the best chance in this tight field, in my opinion. Will stay and will enjoy the pace of the race.

The only mare in the field with winning form here, and that was over 5 furlongs further in December 2024. That experience could hold her in good stead and she should be staying on for each-way appeal.

All 6 career wins have been at this track, with 4 over course and distance. 2 of those course and distance wins have been off higher marks. 5th of 6 when last seen over course and distance here 3 weeks ago in a Class 3, drops in grade to Class 4 and should come on for that latest run which was following an absence of 112 days.

Kiwi Rush is a 5yr-old son of Mahler ex Don't Forsit. Lto over this C&D he won his bumper at 2/1 last month. The second that day Japetus by Sea the Moon has won since at 1/1f at Newcastle this month. He again travels back to Kelso for another bumper where he'll be ridden by Ireland based Mr PW Mullins for H Derham. I think he can continue on his winning ways on this occasion.
Second in this two seasons ago and now looking back to its best, Homme Public looks a each-way steal, if not more, for Oliver Greenall.

Kept on well when winning over this trip at Wetherby last month and is a previous course winner over 2 miles here. Up 4 pounds as a consequence of that recent success, but that is negated by the 7-pound allowance claimed in the saddle by Harry Atkins and of interest effectively 3 pounds below that winning mark.
Looks a great each way bet. In my opinion, it looks to have the best chance under these conditions. A bit out of form, but against this field, I've priced it around 10/3. Looks a top bet.

Looks to have the best chance. However, the race is very hard to predict. Should be around 4/1, so take the each way price while you can. Doesn't have any concerns and looks the best handicapped in the race. Express Sunshine will challenge strongly, however.
Won over this course and distance last year off 2lb higher weight, has been out of form but now looks on a handy weight and likes the course.
Has been very well backed. Had some good form at the start of the season, but since has been disappointing. Could bounce back in these conditions.

The standout bet on the card for me. Has run very well in defeat, and none more so than in a decent listed contest when leading for most of the race but getting headed over the last, finishing a close 3rd. Gets 7lb from her main danger here, and the 2m 4f trip should enable her to see this out in front. Lots to like.

Slightly overpriced. I think the favorite may lose the race as it won't be suited to the trip. I reckon this is the only horse in the race with enough to pick up the pieces. Looks decent value at 2/1 as it should be around 13/8.

Serious Challenge was a very good flat horse, running at pattern level and being rated 102 on his last start. He's shown a good aptitude for hurdles, winning his last two after an educational first start, and beat a good Elliot yardstick by 9L last time out. That came on heavy ground but with his flat pedigree he should relish a return to quicker conditions and a rating of 128 looks to leave loads of scope after just three hurdle starts and his exploits on the level. Yard in really strong form and all set for a big race.
Convincing seven-length victory at Doncaster last on third run out since debut and wind op. Should have no issue here in a handicap race with a strong jockey on board.
Jackpot des Bordes looks very well handicapped on the best of his form. The horse he beat 2 runs ago is now rated 130, which if taken at face value makes the selection look really well treated.

This horse has won 3 of its 5 races to date. Is still unexposed and open to improvement. The form of the win at Wetherby looks decent and with a fair looking handicap mark and decent going a big run could be forthcoming.

Yet to win in 6 races over fences but placed in 3 of those races and all over further. Sent off as favourite for the Plate Handicap Chase at the 2024 Cheltenham Festival over this trip but fell early. Disappointed in 3 races since and not seen since December 2024, but could go well fresh with recent wind surgery offering the potential for improvement.
Came back to form last time out at Huntingdon, has been well backed and looks on a handy mark only 1lb higher than last winning mark.

Another horse who comes in here with plenty to prove at present, but also boasts decent form in the book. The only reservation I would have is the quicker ground. He's only run on it once. To be fair, he ran well on that occasion, beaten 6L by the winner Hunters Yarn, back in 2nd place. He did have Inothewayurthinkin behind him, however. Although he's yet to show any worthwhile form for this stable, he's had his excuses. He likely needed the run on reappearance. He ran okay in the Peter Marsh. I just think the trip stretched him. He struggled off 12st last time out, beaten a distance back in 3rd place. Maybe the weight on soft ground did him in. He's now down to a mark of 139, with the first-time cheekpieces and tongue tie going on. His form for his former stable suggests he's got plenty to give off this type of mark. He did win a Grade 2 novice and also beat the recent Gold Cup winner Inothewayurthinkin in a beginners chase the run before that Grade 2 win.

Comes into this with a bit to prove at present, but very much is a ground-dependent horse. He gets his correct conditions this time, which will help him massively. He's only had 3 chase runs to date. On chase debut, he proved himself to be a chaser to keep on the right side of. He won a 4-runner handicap off this mark at Ascot, beating Bad just over 1L. He showed great battling qualities to repel the challenge of Bad. He also made a crucial mistake at the 2nd last fence. To recover from that and go on to win says a lot about him. He also gave 7 lbs in weight to the winner. That form looks better now with the runner-up winning twice since, with the latest victory coming off a mark of 134. He's pulled up in his 3 runs since. Personally, I don't think he handles soft ground at all, so happy to overlook those runs in the hope the better ground can spark an improved effort. He's got a nice racing weight, which helps. If he can get back to that Ascot form, he looks to have room for maneuver off this type of mark.
PTP winner, first time up to 2m4f and likely to benefit from it. 2nd in a Listed NHF at Cheltenham when staying on well.

Progressive mare that has won her last two, the latest making all to power clear by 11 lengths. That gives her top weight here but she could be good enough to overcome that challenge. The bigger field will help give her a pace to aim at too. Thriving at this distance of 2m4f or thereabouts and no issues with ground conditions. Also has a win to her name at this track in a bumper last season which bodes well. Trainer and jockey combo in cracking form this month.

This horse has shown a decent level of form and is very consistent. She won well at Warwick earlier in the season, and although the stable's second string, she looks to be well-weighted and should handle the underfoot conditions.
Has been running well in hurdles this season and now making a handicap debut. Probably has more improvement to come in these ideal conditions.
Come on Nia, disappointed last time out at Ffos Las on heavy ground. She will be much happier on this quicker surface and is closely handicapped with Crazierthandaisy on her running at Warwick.
Looks a class above these and will enjoy getting back on some decent going. Didn't enjoy the soft going at Wincanton.

Has the potential to be a lot more, and that's the reason for the tip. Should go off shorter (more like 100/30). Looks a cracking each way bet as it's nearly a certainty to get in the frame and is one of the only horses in the race that doesn't have any apparent concerns.

The trainer does well with this profile of horse. Won sole start in France on the flat last September, now owned by the Jago family. Gets considerable weight off the odds-on favorite, carrying just ten stone four pounds. Might reward us at a decent price.

Talk To The Man won his point in impressive fashion. He was well fancied first time out but got bogged down in the testing going. Both Paul Nicholls and Harry Cobden speak well of him, and he could turn out to be a top-class performer.

This is always a very good bumper and was won last year by the highly promising Regents Stroll. There are some very promising looking horses, but I really like the look of My Fortune who has a great pedigree. He is by Milan, out of a Bob Back mare who has produced plenty of good horses. He has been entered numerous times over recent weeks so should be ready to do himself justice in this hot contest.
Overpriced at 40/1 and could easily be involved in the finish. First-time cheekpieces are a plus and is closely matched with Beau Balko.

Another horse who prefers a sounder surface, which he gets today. He's just 2 lbs above his last winning mark, which should help. Although admittedly, he's never won off a mark this high, his overall form would suggest this mark certainly isn't beyond him. He tends to run well at this track. He also boasts a CD win, which helps, of course, having won this race off a 10 lbs lower mark last term. His form this season would suggest he can defy that 10 lbs higher mark. He won a competitive handicap at Chepstow on reappearance, finding plenty to fend off Pull Again Green. He then finished a decent 3rd behind Chianti Classico at Ascot off a 2 lbs higher mark than this, beaten just 4L. His most recent run was okay, finishing a beaten 2nd behind Tightenourbelts. That horse was well in off that mark, plus this fella carried 12 st, so no disgrace there. If he runs his race, he should be thereabouts.

Daaris looks the way to go here was last seen at Lingfield 17 days ago where finishing 5th/9 and did shape better than that bare result suggests with the drop in trip not suiting too on that occasion however he has an extra 1 furlong 219 yards at his disposal here and that will play greatly into his strengths has met a couple of these rivals before in past races and he meets them on better terms this time out jockey Mason Paetel takes off a valuable looking 5lb which only enhances his good looking claims here must be considered in a race of this nature
Winner over course and distance in January. Mostly solid efforts in defeat since including when only beaten a length in 5th last time and very unlikely to be far away once again.

This R. Varian-trained 4-year-old filly won on her racecourse debut over one mile and one furlong at this course back in January last year. After being beaten by 3 3/4 lengths in third of the eight runners behind the well-backed A. M. Balding-trained Turquina over one mile and three furlongs at Southwell, when coming back from a 416-day break, with Aidan Keeley onboard, she can make her presence felt today.

Priced at even money in my books, and 7/2 is up for grabs. Going double stakes for this one as it looks like one of the bets of the week. The closest to it, in my opinion, needs to find another 10 lbs to beat it, and I'm sure it'll go off a lot shorter than this.

An interesting looking class 5 handicap on a Saturday evening with my vote going to Maids Head a very consistent daughter of Pinatubo who was last seen at Kempton 17 days ago where finishing a very respectable 3rd/8 and is most certainly entitled to strip fitter this time out as that was her return run after a 107 day break and should also be a lot sharper at the finish this time out currently operating on an unchanged mark of 68 Maids Head looks poised to strike here and also has a handy draw coming out of gate 2 here at Wolverhampton which should put her in the perfect challenging position and as i metion above she is likely to be a lot sharper at the finish here today jockey Benoit D L Sayette takes the ride and can give Marco Botti's inmate a promising ride here at Wolverhampton very much one to consider . Respected .

I can't resist a small each way bet on this well-drawn horse, which has shown nothing in his last two runs. But prior to that, he was a half-length second on his only previous run over course and distance. The horse led until late on and races off the same mark here. Clearly, a reproduction of that form would make a mockery of the 50/1 quote here. He even has the favorable low draw again, so hopefully, he'll set the pace again and attempt to fend off the late challengers.

In my opinion, it should be around 2/1, so the fact they're offering an each-way price is a complete mystery. Looks a cracking bet and definitely the one to beat in this field. Very enthusiastic, however, and this may lead to it using a wee bit too much energy. The field isn't overly competitive, so it should get the job done in this race even if it does blow a little steam at the beginning.

I think Init Together is overpriced here. Won 4 on the bounce earlier in the year and has been consistent ever since. Back to possibly his best distance, well drawn, and his will to win makes him a bet at these odds.

This 3-year-old colt made a winning racecourse debut for trainer R. Varian over one mile at this course 15 days ago. He ran on well in the closing stages despite showing signs of greenness to beat the well-backed K. R. Burke-trained Nordic Norm by 2 1/4 lengths. With improvement likely and J. Mitchell back in the saddle, he can follow up today.

Billy rides this one and looks to be riding out of his skin before the season starts. The horse looks like one of the ones to beat and with the least concerns out of my three contenders (including Broken Spear, Pallas Lord). They both have trainer concerns and aren't the correct price. This is overpriced and should run a cracking race.

Winner over a mile here in January. Somewhat inconsistent since, but ran okay when not beaten far in 5th last time and is of interest this evening on this rare drop to 7 furlongs, as won over course and distance off 7lb higher just over a year ago.

This ex-Mark Fahey trained 3-year-old colt has been placed in his first two races in Ireland. The latest was over one mile at Dundalk when only beaten by one length in second of the eleven runners behind the A. Murray trained favorite, Ardagh Red. So if fit enough to do himself justice, he can make a winning debut for new trainer G. Boughey.

Gelded son of Magna Grecia who was last seen at this venue over the mile trip 12 days ago where finishing 8th/9 however I'm willing to excuse that run as he looked to be in need of it as he was returning from a 80 day break on the occasion currently operating on a falling mark of 50 Nigel Tinkler's inmate is well off the handicappers radar and it is very well possible he is better than a mark of 50 heading down the handicap route in very good time as he is off the handicappers radar for the time being it would be a wise and profitable move to catch him running well at this stage as he is a valuable looking E/W price at the time of writing jockey Billy Loughnane takes the ride that being a positive booking . Respected .

This Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood trained 5-year-old gelding is the winner of three races from five furlongs to one mile on the all-weather, the latest over one mile at this course 12 days ago. When keeping on well in the closing stages, he beat the M Herrington trained Anif by 1 1/4 lengths. So with D Nolan doing the steering, he has a good chance to follow up tonight.

South Shore's form on paper does look off putting however looks can be deceiving and a deeper analysis of this individual tells a whole different story was last seen at this venue racing at the 6 furlong trip where finishing last of 8 however he was returning from a 152 day break and most certainly needed that run likely to be more adjusted back home as he joined this yard last year from the Karl Burke stable and he did win of a mark of 75 with that stable he is now operating on mark 68 now surely a 4yo gelded son of Blue Point who was capable of winning of a mark of 75 last year is likely to have a very big performance in the locker of a mark of 68 and he did switch yards at a crucial stage of his career a monster E/W price at the time of writing he is worth the interest and if on song as he should be he could cause a shock in the finale and if he is to settle for a silver medal at the very least it wouldn't be so bad given the odds on offer
